title: Python: the walker misses two binding kinds (PEP 695 'type m = ...' and 'with ctx() as (m, n)' tuple targets), so a name looks unbound
description: Found by the Opus review of #159 (GCLI-100, D1) at 29c775e5, PRE-EXISTING (wrong-edge direction: a binding is missed, so a name looks unbound or singly bound). Probed by the worker on dev abea54f with class B: def m; class C(B): <body>; C().m(): (1) class body 'type m = int' (PEP 695 type alias statement): the walker records no binding, so C().m() still gets an edge to B.m (1 edge; control 'm = None' gives 0); (2) class body 'with ctx() as (m, n): pass': addAsPatternBinding takes only direct identifier children (calls.ts around 1035-1045), so the tuple target binds nothing and the edge to B.m is kept (1 edge). Both make a name look unbound where Python binds it, and every single-binding rule (E1, N3, D1 and the bare-call enumeration) relies on the walker. Match capture patterns are GCLI-101 (D2), not here. Not built: routed to opum-doc through the leader first. Probe first for further forms (with-as list targets, nested tuples, starred), then red-before fixtures per hole, fix, mutation checks, per-site re-measure of the five pins.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a class-body type alias statement and a with-as tuple (or list, nested, starred) target are each recorded as a binding, with red-before fixtures
each hole has a mutation check that goes red
a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with any in-repo edge it removes named
